questions.question: How is linear momentum calculated for an object?
Which unit can express momentum?
What is impulse?
choices: The change in momentum caused by a force over time
The distance traveled during a collision
The total kinetic energy of every object
The mass lost in a collision

questions.question: What does an elastic collision conserve in an isolated system?
What characterizes a perfectly inelastic collision?
choices: The objects must have equal initial speeds

questions.question: Why is momentum a vector quantity?
choices: It depends only on elapsed time
It is measured only in kilograms
It has no relationship to velocity
It includes direction as well as magnitude

questions.question: What is recoil?
choices: Motion caused only by a change in volume
Backward motion associated with another object's forward momentum

questions.question: When is a system's total momentum conserved?
choices: When every object's speed is zero
When its net external impulse is zero
When all objects have the same mass

questions.question: Why can total momentum stay constant while kinetic energy decreases in a collision?
choices: Momentum conservation requires constant kinetic energy
Lost kinetic energy becomes negative mass
Some kinetic energy becomes thermal energy, sound, or deformation
Momentum measures energy in different units

questions.question: Why can increasing stopping time reduce average force for the same momentum change?
choices: The same impulse is spread over a longer interval
Longer time increases the object's initial momentum
Impulse becomes zero whenever time increases

questions.question: How do the forces between two colliding objects compare during their interaction?
choices: The heavier object always exerts the greater force
They are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
Only the faster object exerts a force
The forces always point in the same direction

questions.question: Why can two objects have equal momentum but different kinetic energies?
choices: Momentum depends on mv, while kinetic energy depends on ½mv²
Equal momentum requires equal masses and speeds
Kinetic energy depends only on direction
Momentum cannot describe more than one object

questions.question: How does doubling velocity at fixed mass affect momentum?
Why must signs or directions be included when adding momenta?
choices: Momentum cannot be added for different masses
Every moving object contributes a positive scalar only
Opposite directions contribute oppositely to the vector total

questions.question: Why is a collision analysis sometimes only approximately isolated?
choices: A system is isolated whenever both objects have equal masses
External forces may act, but their collision-time impulse can be small
A system is isolated whenever kinetic energy decreases
Any collision automatically excludes external forces

questions.question: A 3 kg cart moves east at 4 m/s. What is its momentum?
A constant net force of 5 N acts for 2 s. What is the impulse?
Equal-mass carts have equal speeds in opposite directions. What is their combined momentum?
choices: A value determined only by their kinetic energies
